sides.text: A company wants to enforce encryption and remote wipe on employee smartphones. Which solution fits?
D. MDM

more.text: Mobile device management enforces policy and remote wipe on phones.

sides.text: Employees choose a laptop from an approved list that the company owns. Which model is this?
D. CYOD

more.text: CYOD lets employees pick from approved company devices.

sides.text: Which Wi-Fi standard uses SAE to resist offline password cracking?
A. WPA3

more.text: WPA3 replaces the PSK handshake with SAE.

sides.text: Which cookie flag stops JavaScript from reading a session cookie?
D. HttpOnly

more.text: HttpOnly blocks script access. Secure limits it to HTTPS.

sides.text: A scan logs in to servers to check installed patches. Which type of scan is this?
A. Credentialed scan

more.text: Credentialed scans see patches and settings accurately.

sides.text: A vulnerability scanner reports a flaw on a host that is already patched. What is this?
A. False positive

more.text: A false positive reports a problem that doesn't exist.

sides.text: A flaw has a CVSS score of 9.8. How is it rated?
C. Critical

more.text: CVSS 9.0 to 10.0 is Critical.

sides.text: A vendor can't patch quickly, so a WAF rule blocks exploitation in the meantime. What is this?
A. Compensating control

more.text: A WAF rule stands in for the missing patch.

sides.text: Which tool aggregates and correlates logs from many sources to alert on attacks?
D. SIEM

more.text: A SIEM centralizes and correlates security logs.

sides.text: A DNS record lists the mail servers allowed to send for a domain. Which email control is this?
C. SPF

more.text: SPF lists authorized sending servers.

sides.text: Which email control tells receivers to reject messages that fail SPF and DKIM alignment?
B. DMARC

more.text: DMARC sets the policy for authentication failures.

sides.text: A tool records process behavior on laptops and can isolate an infected one. Which is it?
B. EDR

more.text: EDR monitors endpoint behavior and enables response actions.

sides.text: A user logs in once and opens several applications without re-entering credentials. Which is this?
A. SSO

more.text: Single sign-on authenticates once for many apps.

sides.text: Which protocol lets an app access a user's resources through tokens without the password?
C. OAuth

more.text: OAuth delegates authorization with tokens.

sides.text: Which access control model decides based on attributes of the user, resource, and environment?
B. ABAC

more.text: ABAC evaluates multiple attributes against policy.

sides.text: Admins receive elevated rights for two hours, after which the rights expire automatically. Which approach is this?
D. Just-in-time permissions

more.text: JIT grants temporary privilege and then revokes it.

sides.text: Which authentication method is phishing-resistant and uses hardware with public-key cryptography?
D. FIDO2 security key

more.text: FIDO2 keys verify the site, so phishing doesn't work.

sides.text: Which incident response phase removes malware and closes the entry point?
C. Eradication

more.text: Eradication removes the cause. Containment only limits the spread.

sides.text: Which data should be collected first according to the order of volatility?
C. RAM

more.text: More volatile data is lost first, so RAM comes before disk.

sides.text: Everyone who handled a hard drive signs a log. What is this called?
B. Chain of custody

more.text: Chain of custody documents who handled evidence and when.

sides.text: Analysts search logs for signs of an attacker before any alert fires. Which activity is this?
B. Threat hunting

more.text: Threat hunting proactively looks for hidden compromise.

sides.text: Which log source shows which device held a given IP address at a certain time?
A. DHCP or network logs

more.text: DHCP logs map IP addresses to devices over time.

sides.text: A SOAR playbook calls a firewall API to block an IP automatically. Which benefit does this show?
A. Faster reaction time

more.text: Automation responds in seconds. The other options are considerations, not benefits.

sides.text: A retired server's drives are cryptographically erased so they can be reused. Which process is this?
D. Sanitization

more.text: Sanitization removes data while allowing media to be reused.

sides.text: A device without current patches is placed on a restricted VLAN until it's fixed. Which technology is this?
C. NAC

more.text: NAC checks device posture before granting full access.
